channel.title: Cadence Evidence — PT Research Signal
channel.description: Daily curated physical therapy & rehab research for clinicians. AI-scored signal from 56 sources.

item.title: Rehabilitation of Athletes With Hamstring Strain Injury: SONAFE-Brazil Clinical Practice Guideline.
item.description: The National Society of Sports Physical Therapy (SONAFE-Brazil) released a clinical practice guideline for hamstring strain injury rehabilitation, utilizing the GRADE approach to synthesize evidence from randomized clinical trials for clinicians and athletes.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Percutaneous Electrolysis for the Management of Musculoskeletal Disorders. A Systematic Review With Meta-Analysis.
item.description: A systematic review and meta-analysis of 13 trials found that adding percutaneous electrolysis (PNE) to therapeutic exercise (TE) was not superior to sham plus TE or TE alone for pain or function in tendinopathies. Low-certainty evidence suggested PNE combined with TE might offer greater short- to medium-term pain reduction compared to dry needling plus TE in tendinopathy, but not in myofascial pain syndrome.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Reframing hands-on musculoskeletal assessment as a measurement instrument rather than a technique debate: a theoretical framework applying COSMIN to HODA-A.
item.description: This theoretical paper proposes a Hands-On Data Acquisition and Analysis (HODA-A) framework, applying COSMIN principles to conceptualize hands-on musculoskeletal assessment as a clinician-reported outcome measurement process rather than isolated manual techniques.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Effects of thoracic kinesiological taping on pulmonary functions, respiratory muscle strength, and functional independence in patients with hemiplegia: a randomized controlled clinical trial.
item.description: A randomized controlled trial (n=30) found that thoracic kinesiology taping combined with conventional rehabilitation significantly improved pulmonary function (FVC, FEV1, PEF) and maximal inspiratory pressure, as well as Functional Independence Measure scores, in individuals with chronic post-stroke hemiplegia.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Comparison of kinesio taping and myofascial release therapy in cervicogenic headache: a randomized controlled trial.
item.description: A randomized controlled trial (n=81) found that both kinesio taping and myofascial release, combined with home exercise, effectively reduced pain and headache frequency in cervicogenic headache. MFR provided more sustained improvements in disability and physical quality of life.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Is Reduced Spinal Range of Motion a Prognostic Factor for Pain Intensity, Disability, and Global Recovery in People With Specific or Nonspecific Spinal Pain? A Systematic Review.
item.description: A systematic review of 37 studies found very low certainty evidence regarding whether reduced spinal range of motion is a prognostic factor for pain, disability, or recovery in spinal pain patients, with inconsistent results and all studies rated as high risk of bias.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Effect of iTBS and rTMS Combined with Robotic Rehabilitation on Ambulation and Lower Extremity Motor Function in Chronic SCI Patients.
item.description: An RCT found that intermittent theta-burst stimulation (iTBS) and repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS) combined with robotic rehabilitation improved ambulation and lower extremity motor function in chronic spinal cord injury patients compared to sham, with no significant differences between active protocols.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Shear wave elastography for assessing lower extremity muscle stiffness after anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction: A systematic review.
item.description: A systematic review concluded that shear wave elastography can detect muscle-specific stiffness deficits after ACL reconstruction, including reduced vastus medialis and semitendinosus stiffness, which correlate with function beyond strength, but standardized protocols are required for clinical guidance.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: A Return to Performance Continuum for Football (Soccer) Players After ACL Reconstruction: Bridging Rehabilitation, Return to Play and Sustained Performance.
item.description: A paper outlines a staged Return to Performance continuum for football players after ACL reconstruction, bridging rehabilitation and sustained performance. It emphasizes restoring movement quality, progressive football-specific technical/tactical retraining, physical reconditioning, and maximal strength restoration.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Digital therapeutic combining exercise and cognitive-behavioural therapy reduces pain in patients with chronic patellofemoral pain: a multicentre randomised controlled trial
item.description: A multicenter randomized controlled trial found that a smartphone-based multidisciplinary intervention combining personalized exercise and cognitive-behavioral therapy significantly improved pain, function, quality of life, and psychological well-being in patients with chronic patellofemoral pain. This digital therapeutic offers a scalable and cost-efficient delivery of care aligned with clinical guidelines.
item.author: BJSM

item.title: The effects of route previewing on adaptive gait and gaze behaviour under cognitive dual-task conditions in older adults
item.description: This study found that cognitive dual-tasking increased stepping errors and reduced stride length, but route previewing significantly mitigated these negative effects on adaptive gait and gaze behavior. Previewing prior to gait initiation helped participants look further ahead and make fewer irrelevant fixations, improving walking safety under cognitive load.
item.author: medRxiv

item.title: Transcutaneous Vagus Nerve Stimulation Improves Motor Function of Upper Extremity in Adults with Chronic Ischemic Stroke: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
item.description: A randomized controlled trial found that transcutaneous auricular vagal nerve stimulation (taVNS) combined with upper limb exercises led to significant improvements in Fugl-Meyer Assessment for Upper Extremity (FMA-UE: MD = 3.95, 95% CI 0.21-7.69) and shoulder/elbow muscle strength in chronic ischemic stroke patients compared to sham taVNS.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Sex- and age-specific normative values for lower-limb field tests in elite TeamGym gymnasts.
item.description: A cross-sectional study of 216 elite TeamGym gymnasts established sex- and age-specific normative values for ankle dorsiflexion, hop for distance, height-adjusted hop for distance, side-hop, and heel-raise performance. Significant sex × age-group interactions were observed for hop outcomes, with senior males outperforming junior males and senior females showing no age-group differences.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Graft type is not associated with revision ACL reconstruction in football players: a nationwide cohort analysis of subsequent ACL reconstructions
item.description: A nationwide cohort analysis of more than 10 000 football players who underwent ACL reconstruction found that graft choice (hamstring, patellar tendon, or quadriceps tendon autograft) was not associated with the risk of revision ACL reconstruction among players who returned to competition, in either women or men.
item.author: BJSM

item.title: Effect of Integrated Respiratory and Functional Training on Weaning from Mechanical Ventilation, Respiratory and Peripheral Muscle Strength, Functional Ability, and Pain After Emergency Abdominal Surgery: A Randomized Controlled Trial
item.description: A randomized controlled trial investigated the effect of integrated respiratory and functional training on weaning from mechanical ventilation, respiratory and peripheral muscle strength, functional ability, and pain after emergency abdominal surgery. The study aims to address respiratory impairment and prolonged hospitalization common in these patients.
item.author: Archives of PM&R

item.title: How does pre-stroke physical activity influence physical activity one year after minor stroke, and what role does cognitive impairment play?
item.description: A secondary analysis of 100 minor stroke patients found that low pre-stroke physical activity was associated with higher odds of low physical activity 12 months post-stroke (OR=5.81, 95% CI: 1.61-24.0, p=0.010), suggesting its utility in identifying at-risk patients.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Dextrose prolotherapy for chronic symptomatic rotator cuff tendinopathy and subacromial bursitis: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
item.description: A systematic review and meta-analysis of 14 studies found very low certainty evidence that dextrose prolotherapy offers little to no benefit for chronic rotator cuff tendinopathy/bursitis compared to saline, and may result in worse physical performance compared to corticosteroid injections.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Patients' experiences of participating in physiotherapeutic telerehabilitation for postpartum pelvic floor dysfunction; a qualitative study.
item.description: A qualitative study exploring patients' experiences with physiotherapeutic telerehabilitation for postpartum pelvic floor dysfunction found it was perceived as a complementary tool that improves accessibility and flexibility, but highlighted the need for advanced digital communication and concerns about the lack of physical examination.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: The enhanced rehabilitation programme for significant musculoskeletal injuries from the manchester arena bombing - A process evaluation study investigating patients' and physiotherapists' experiences.
item.description: A process evaluation of an enhanced rehabilitation program for major trauma survivors found it beneficial for recovery and motivation but identified challenges in sustaining progress and transitioning to standard care, indicating a need for improved long-term rehabilitation pathways.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: First aggression as a planning signal in post-acute stroke rehabilitation: Service benchmarks, goal setting, and a 60-day precaution window from a comprehensive observational cohort.
item.description: An observational study in post-acute stroke rehabilitation established service benchmarks following the first aggression event, indicating a 60-day precaution window and functional gaps to inform goal setting and discharge planning, though multicenter validation is needed.
item.author: PubMed
